correctness.rationale: Exact quotient-metric reduction gives U uniform and V independent triangular. All p>0: the moment integral is strictly log-convex in log aspect ratio and coercive, hence has one optimizer; antisymmetric integration shows q<1. Direct moment algebra verifies q2, q4 and normalized minimum values. Uniform Lp limit localizes q_p near one; endpoint Laplace rescaling with triangular density gives the rigorous high-power correction 2/p. The standalone checker independently tests quadrature and simulated distances but the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The fixed-area surface-shape question is naturally motivated by intrinsic random routing costs. The theorem supplies one sharp optimizer for every real p>0, two distinct exact even-power benchmarks preventing any universal power-optimum shape, and a nontrivial first large-power correction arising from the vanishing axial-difference density at maximal separation. A continuum of constrained geometric metric optimizations is characterized, not just a normalization identity.
